rationale: Evidence from iteration 1 (entityR2A, 60 trials): the oval finished 19 of 20 trials at mean time 1.88 s, but the s-bend and slalom still ended off_track with progress 0.39 and 0.17. Max error sat at about 0.062 to 0.064 m, at the 0.06 m limit, with about one line-loss event per run. steering_oscillation was about 0.21 on every track, above the 0.15 threshold the Evaluator gave. Widening the sensors and lowering kp fixed the straight-line finishing but not the tight bends. The high jitter points to a turn command that is still too aggressive or underdamped, while the line loss on the sharper bends points to the robot carrying too much speed into them. This candidate makes three controller changes and keeps the geometry fixed, so the race can attribute the outcome to the controller. (1) kd rises from 0.3 to 0.4, following the Evaluator's guidance to damp jitter above 0.15. (2) kp rises from 1.2 to 1.4, a small step back toward the level where iteration 0 lost the line less often on the bends, since the Evaluator's rule for line loss near 0.06 m is to raise kp. The kd increase offsets the extra gain. (3) base_speed drops from 1.2 to 1.0, which gives the robot more time to correct on the s-bend and slalom. The oval has margin: at 1.88 s with base 1.2, a lower speed should still finish under 3 s, though completion time will rise. Expected result: lower steering_oscillation (below about 0.15), no off_track ends on the s-bend and slalom, and line_loss_events near zero. If the robot still loses the line with low oscillation, the next step is kp toward 1.6. If it finishes with completion_time above 3 s, raise base_speed toward 1.3. Geometry stays unchanged until the controller is tuned on the widened sensor spread.
